1: a counter-shot shows the target aiming back: the crosshair becomes one pole of a duel
the watcher's purpose (spy or guardian) becomes the question: one look, two situations
the car's movement, not the driver's seat, organises the frame: the centre begins to flow
the ship shrinks to a speck in a vast sea: the gaze reveals its own smallness
the glide carries the view rather than a subject owning it
the face stops being the one who sees and becomes the surface that is seen
2: the passengers become the fixed centre from which the river is seen
the corridor empties of any destination: space for its own sake
the camera locks onto one walker's back and the centre solidifies
the water's flicker takes over and no vessel or viewer anchors it
the crowd shares one affect (faces turned, a common expression)
the drift settles into an establishing survey of a determinate workplace
3: the multiplied discs reflect one actual image: mirrors face to face
the cell reads as the seed of an environment to come
the flow carries a centre along (a boat, a swimmer)
the rows read as a habitual series whose units matter
the pattern has to be deciphered as something else
the shot is held for a watcher who cannot act on what they see
4: a reverse shot makes him the one whose view organises the world
we can no longer tell whether she is falling into a dream
the face is only a seer before a situation it cannot answer
the lines read as the world's imprint driving a coming action
the expression is seized by a drive about to break out
the pain becomes a primal force acting through the body
5: no single bird stays legible within the flock
the crowd is only the setting for someone else's action
the screen they face matters more than their shared attention
the posture of waiting, not a shared affect, is what we see
